part_1_quantum_redesign.title: Cloud-9 Quantum A_c Redesign v3.0 — Message-Sensitive Complexity
part_1_quantum_redesign.motivation: v1/v2 quantum A_c failed validation because I = n_states × 256 is a constant determined by Hilbert space dimension, not dynamical complexity. The circuit (H⊗⁵ + measure) never encoded the message. A_c varied <0.1% across all messages.
design_principles: PRINCIPLE 1: A_c must vary >10% when message content changes
PRINCIPLE 2: Each component must be sensitive to the OUTPUT distribution, not just circuit width
PRINCIPLE 3: Null model (uniform random) must produce A_c ≈ 0, not A_c ≈ 1641
PRINCIPLE 4: Message encoding must be PART of the circuit, not external to it
PRINCIPLE 5: Components must have physical interpretations testable on simulator

new_formula.normalization: All components normalized to [0, 1] range; A_c_quantum ∈ [0, 5]

H_q (Hierarchical_Complexity).old_definition: Topological entropy of measurement graph — insensitive to distribution
H_q (Hierarchical_Complexity).new_definition: Normalized mutual information I(message; measurement) = H(message) + H(measurement) - H(message, measurement)
H_q (Hierarchical_Complexity).computation: Compute classical mutual information between input bitstring (message) and output bitstring (measurement) over N shots. Normalize by H(message) to get [0,1].
H_q (Hierarchical_Complexity).physical_meaning: How much information about the message is preserved in the quantum measurement
H_q (Hierarchical_Complexity).test: For H⊗⁵ + measure with NO message encoding: H_q = 0. For amplitude-encoded message: H_q > 0

P_q (Phase_Space_Perturbation).old_definition: KL divergence from uniform — but uniform WAS the output
P_q (Phase_Space_Perturbation).new_definition: Jensen-Shannon divergence between output distribution P(message) and uniform distribution U, weighted by circuit depth
P_q (Phase_Space_Perturbation).computation: JS(P||U) × (1 - e^(-depth/10)) where depth = number of non-trivial gates
P_q (Phase_Space_Perturbation).physical_meaning: How much the circuit structure perturbs the uniform random baseline
P_q (Phase_Space_Perturbation).test: H⊗⁵ + measure: depth=0 → P_q = 0. QAOA with 4 layers: P_q > 0

I_q (Dynamical_Instability).old_definition: I = n_states × 256 = CONSTANT — the fatal flaw
I_q (Dynamical_Instability).new_definition: Effective participation ratio: PR = 1 / Σ_i p_i² where p_i are measurement probabilities. Normalized: I_q = log(PR) / log(n_states)
I_q (Dynamical_Instability).computation: From measured counts, estimate probabilities p_i = count_i / N_shots. Compute PR. Take log ratio.
I_q (Dynamical_Instability).physical_meaning: How many states effectively participate in the dynamics. PR=1 (single state) → I_q=0. PR=n_states (full uniform) → I_q=1.
I_q (Dynamical_Instability).interpretation: LOW I_q means dynamics collapsed to few states (high instability). HIGH I_q means uniform exploration (stable mixing).
I_q (Dynamical_Instability).test: For H⊗⁵: I_q ≈ 1.0 (uniform). For Grover's algorithm: I_q << 1.0 (concentrated)

F_q (Information_Fragmentation).new_definition: Normalized entropy production rate: F_q = (S_output - S_input) / S_max where S = von Neumann entropy of density matrix
F_q (Information_Fragmentation).computation: Estimate output density matrix from tomography or use classical entropy S = -Σ p_i log(p_i). Compare to input entropy.
F_q (Information_Fragmentation).physical_meaning: How much the circuit fragments/encrypts information. Positive = entropy production (mixing). Negative = entropy reduction (purification).
F_q (Information_Fragmentation).test: Depolarizing channel: F_q > 0. Error correction: F_q < 0

\u03b1_q (Temporal_Acceleration).new_definition: Coherence decay rate: α_q = exp(-t_gate / T_2*) where T_2* is measured coherence time
\u03b1_q (Temporal_Acceleration).computation: Run same circuit at increasing depths. Fit exponential decay of H_q vs depth. Extract characteristic decay depth.
\u03b1_q (Temporal_Acceleration).physical_meaning: How quickly quantum coherence (and thus message sensitivity) decays due to noise
\u03b1_q (Temporal_Acceleration).test: Simulator (no noise): α_q = 1.0. IBM hardware: α_q < 1.0, depth-dependent

required_circuit_changes.message_encoding: MUST use amplitude encoding or angle embedding: |ψ⟩ = Σ_i m_i |i⟩ where m_i are message amplitudes
required_circuit_changes.circuit_family: Use parameterized circuits: QAOA, VQE ansatz, or hardware-efficient ansatz with message-dependent parameters

layers: Layer 0: Angle embedding — Rz(message_i) on each qubit
Layer 3: Measurement — all qubits in Z basis
example_circuit.parameters: θ₁, θ₂ optimized to maximize H_q for given message
example_circuit.expected_behavior: Different messages → different optimal θ → different output distributions → different A_c

tests: Test A: Same message, same circuit → A_c consistent within 5%
Test B: Different messages, same circuit → A_c varies >20%
Test C: Random message vs structured message → structured has higher H_q
Test D: Null circuit (no message encoding) → A_c ≈ 0.5 ± 0.2

step_2_noisy_simulator.tool: Qiskit Aer with noise model from IBM backend
tests: Test E: A_c decreases monotonically with added depolarizing noise
Test F: α_q correctly estimates coherence decay rate
Test G: Message sensitivity H_q persists at realistic noise levels
Test H: Run same circuit 5 times → A_c reproducible within 10%
Test I: Run with 3 different messages → A_c significantly different (ANOVA p<0.05)
Test J: Compare to null model (random circuits) → A_c > 2σ above null mean

risk_assessment.risk_1: Amplitude encoding requires classical pre-processing — may introduce artificial structure
risk_assessment.mitigation_1: Use multiple encoding schemes (angle, amplitude, basis) and require consistency
risk_assessment.risk_2: Mutual information estimation is noisy with finite shots
risk_assessment.mitigation_2: Require N_shots ≥ 8192 for H_q; use Bayesian entropy estimation
risk_assessment.risk_3: Hardware noise may dominate signal, making all messages look similar
risk_assessment.mitigation_3: Use error mitigation (ZNE, PEC) or focus on NISQ-friendly circuits with <20 depth

timeline.week_1: Implement v3 formula in Qiskit simulator
timeline.week_4: If Steps 1-2 pass: submit to IBM hardware and run Step 3
timeline.week_5: If Step 3 passes: publish as C9-2026-QUANTUM-VALIDATED-001

part_2_tng_merger_hypothesis.title: Cloud-9 TNG Hypothesis Pivot: Merger-Driven Complexity Evolution
part_2_tng_merger_hypothesis.status: HYPOTHESIS — Ready for TNG API Testing
part_2_tng_merger_hypothesis.motivation: Quiescent halo deficit hypothesis failed (p=0.224, p=0.551). A_c shows no significant difference between quiescent and active halos. However, merger history analysis revealed counter-intuitive pattern: earlier formation redshift → LOWER present-day A_c. This suggests complexity is CREATED by mergers and ERASED by relaxation over cosmic time.

core_hypothesis.statement: Dark matter halo complexity A_c evolves through a CREATE-DESTROY cycle: mergers inject complexity via dynamical perturbation; subsequent relaxation/phase-mixing erases it. The equilibrium A_c is determined by the balance between merger rate and relaxation rate.
core_hypothesis.prediction_1: Halos in high-density environments (frequent mergers) maintain higher A_c
core_hypothesis.prediction_2: Isolated halos (rare mergers) show declining A_c with time since last merger
core_hypothesis.prediction_3: Post-merger A_c peaks at pericentric passage, then decays exponentially
core_hypothesis.prediction_4: A_c correlates with substructure fraction more strongly than with mass

complexity_creation.process: Gravitational torques inject non-equilibrium phase-space structure; streams, shells, and caustics form
complexity_creation.signature: A_c increases rapidly; substructure fraction peaks; velocity anisotropy becomes radial

complexity_destruction.process: Non-equilibrium structures shear out and mix; phase-space density homogenizes
complexity_destruction.timescale: τ_relax ~ 10-20 dynamical times (~5-10 Gyr for MW-mass halos)
complexity_destruction.signature: A_c decreases exponentially; substructure fraction declines; velocity distribution becomes isotropic

equilibrium.result: A_c fluctuates around mean value determined by environment density
equilibrium.field_halos: Low merger rate → A_c below equilibrium, slowly declining
equilibrium.cluster_halos: High merger rate → A_c near equilibrium, high variance

prediction_A.statement: A_c correlates with time_since_last_major_merger with negative slope
prediction_A.test: For each halo, extract merger tree; identify last major merger; correlate A_c vs Δt
prediction_A.expected: Pearson r < -0.3, p < 0.01 for n > 500 halos

prediction_B.statement: A_c correlates with local overdensity more strongly than with mass
prediction_B.test: Compute local density contrast δ = (ρ_local - ρ_mean) / ρ_mean for each halo; compare A_c(δ) vs A_c(M)
prediction_B.expected: |r(A_c, δ)| > |r(A_c, M)|; partial correlation shows δ dominates when M is controlled

prediction_C.statement: A_c peaks at merger pericenter then decays
prediction_C.test: Track A_c along individual merger tree branches; compute A_c at snapshots before/during/after merger
prediction_C.expected: A_c(t) shows peak at pericenter, exponential decay with τ_relax afterward
prediction_C.null: A_c is constant along branch (no merger effect)

prediction_D.statement: Substructure fraction f_sub is a better A_c predictor than concentration c_NFW
prediction_D.test: Compute f_sub from subhalo catalogs; compare predictive power of f_sub vs c_NFW for A_c
prediction_D.expected: R²(A_c ~ f_sub) > R²(A_c ~ c_NFW) by factor > 2

prediction_E.statement: Field halos (isolated) show lower A_c than cluster halos at same mass
prediction_E.test: Split sample by environment (field vs cluster); compare A_c at fixed mass bin
prediction_E.expected: A_c_cluster > A_c_field at same M, significant at p < 0.05
prediction_E.null: No environmental dependence at fixed mass

methodology.data_source: TNG100-1 (or TNG300-1 for larger sample) full merger trees + snapshot particle data
variables_to_extract: Merger tree: all progenitors, mass ratios, merger times
Time since last major merger Δt_last
Local overdensity δ (smoothed on 5 Mpc/h scale)
Spin parameter λ = J|E|^0.5 / G M^2.5
Tidal field eigenvalues at halo position

a_c_computation.note: Use EXISTING v2.1 formula for consistency, but ADD environmental context vector

new_components.E_env (Environmental_Context): Weighted sum of local density, tidal field, and merger rate, normalized to [0,1]
new_components.T_dyn (Dynamical_Age): Time since last major merger / relaxation time, clipped to [0,1]

a_c_computation.revised_formula: A_c_total = [H + P + I + F + α] × (1 + w_env × E_env) × exp(-T_dyn / τ_norm)

test_1_correlation_matrix.method: Pearson/Spearman correlation between A_c and all predictor variables
test_1_correlation_matrix.expected: Strongest correlations: f_sub (+), Δt_last (-), δ (+), Γ_merge (+)

test_2_partial_correlation.method: Partial correlation r(A_c, predictor | M) controlling for mass
test_2_partial_correlation.expected: f_sub and Δt_last remain significant after mass control; mass correlation drops

test_3_merger_tree_tracking.method: For 100 randomly selected major mergers, track A_c(progenitor), A_c(peak), A_c(post)
test_3_merger_tree_tracking.model: Fit A_c(t) = A_c^pre + ΔA_c × exp(-(t-t_merge)/τ_relax) × Θ(t > t_merge)
test_3_merger_tree_tracking.significance: F-test for model vs constant; p < 0.001
test_3_merger_tree_tracking.expected: τ_relax ≈ 5-8 Gyr for MW-mass halos; ΔA_c ≈ 0.05-0.10

test_4_environmental_split.method: T-test comparing A_c(field) vs A_c(cluster) at fixed mass bins
test_4_environmental_split.significance: p < 0.05 in at least 3 of 5 mass bins
test_4_environmental_split.expected: Cluster halos have higher A_c at all masses

test_5_machine_learning.method: Train Random Forest to predict A_c from all variables; extract feature importance
test_5_machine_learning.expected: Top features: f_sub, Δt_last, δ, Γ_merge — NOT mass or concentration

scenario_A_full_support.implication: Merger-driven complexity evolution is real. A_c is a dynamical tracer, not just mass proxy. Publish as C9-2026-COSMO-MERGER-001 (Layer 1).

scenario_B_partial_support.implication: Mechanism is partially correct but needs refinement. May need to include baryonic effects (feedback, AGN). Publish as Layer 2 with caveats.

scenario_C_null_result.implication: A_c formula is fundamentally flawed for cosmology. Need complete redesign or abandon cosmological application. Archive as failed hypothesis.

scenario_D_unexpected.description: Completely different pattern emerges (e.g., A_c anti-correlates with mergers)
scenario_D_unexpected.implication: New physics or new definition of complexity needed. Most interesting outcome scientifically.

connection_to_quantum.analogy: Both quantum and cosmological A_c suffer from 'baseline dominance' — quantum: circuit width; cosmology: mass.
connection_to_quantum.unified_lesson: A_c must measure DEVIATION from equilibrium, not absolute magnitude. In quantum: deviation from uniform. In cosmology: deviation from relaxed NFW.
connection_to_quantum.cross_pollination: The relaxation timescale τ_relax in cosmology is analogous to coherence time T_2* in quantum. Both represent the rate at which structure/information is lost.
connection_to_quantum.formula_unification: Consider defining A_c universally as: A_c = Σ_i (observed_i - equilibrium_i)² / variance_i — a chi-squared-like measure of non-equilibrium

cross_connection.unified_insight: Both quantum and cosmological A_c suffered from 'baseline dominance' — measuring the wrong thing. Quantum: circuit width (I = constant). Cosmology: mass (A_c ∝ M). The fix is the same: measure DEVIATION from equilibrium, not absolute magnitude.
cross_connection.quantum_equilibrium: Uniform random distribution over measurement outcomes
cross_connection.cosmological_equilibrium: Relaxed NFW profile with isotropic velocities
